blog/en/the-most-enjoyable-way-to-keep-y.title: Fun routines for a brain that stays young
panels: It's on the tip of my tongue…
When the word you meant to say keeps vanishing, you start to worry about your brain.
Neuroplasticity responds to new stimulation regardless of age.
Hands-on music and art and learning a foreign language switch the brain back on.
Sleep is the brain's cleaning time, and connecting with people nourishes the hippocampus.

blog/en/nature-heals-the-brain-15-minute.title: 15 minutes in nature reboots the brain
panels: Spending directed attention on work and phones all day wears out the prefrontal cortex.
Rustling leaves and birdsong engage effortless soft fascination.
Start with a 15-minute walk, a plant on your desk, and 5 minutes gazing out the window.
Cortisol drops, and attention, memory, and emotional balance recover.

blog/en/weak-willpower-muscle-aerobic-vs.title: Was muscle behind weak willpower?
panels: I believed exercise was for the body and books were for the brain.
Muscles release myokines that lower inflammation and slow brain aging.
Running supports the hippocampus and BDNF; lifting supports the prefrontal cortex. Do both.
The brain function closest to willpower grows stronger, and crystallized intelligence is protected.

blog/en/burnout-the-brain-needs-a-switch.title: The brain needs a switch, not persuasion
panels: No matter how often I repeated my resolutions, the burnout didn't lift.
Optogenetics: shine light on channelrhodopsin and a brain circuit switches on.
Wellness routines like 30 seconds of visualization before exercise act directly on brain circuits.
Actions that switch on the reward circuit come before resolutions.

blog/en/pro-gamer-brain-mri-trained-brai.title: A trained brain chooses better
panels: How did the brains of pro gamers who play 10 hours a day change?
MRIs of 23 LCK players: the insula and anterior cingulate cortex changed toward "choosing better."
Rehearse in your head first, focus on internal senses, and favor output over input.
What changes the brain is not the amount of time but the structure of training.

blog/en/brain-coordinate-systems-exercis.title: Learning with your own body as the origin
panels: Exercising by watching only your form in the mirror, without feeling it, invites injury.
The brain processes the world in allocentric and egocentric coordinates at once.
Mind-Muscle Connection: bring your attention to the feeling of the muscle you're using.
Embodied learning, like memorizing while walking, stays longer in the hippocampus.

blog/en/sunlight-focus-and-brain-functio.title: Sunlight before coffee
panels: When focus slips, we reach for coffee first.
Cells in the eye take in light to wake the brain; bright daylight made reaction times 7–10% faster.
Build a routine of getting sunlight outdoors in the morning and during the day.
Your circadian rhythm aligns, and focus returns along with dopamine.

blog/en/new-path-for-dementia-treatment-.title: When poison becomes medicine
panels: When the brain's immune cells can't clear amyloid, the risk of dementia rises.
Microglia are the brain's cleaners. A KIST–Boston University team found a new pathway.
Quinolinic acid, known as a toxin, boosts their cleaning ability at low concentrations.
Hormesis, the idea that moderate stress builds resilience, is leading into treatment research.

blog/en/brain-fog-chronic-fatigue-brain-.title: Brain fog: the problem is brain immunity
panels: If your head stays foggy and your stomach bloated even after good sleep, it may be a different signal.
Glial cells (microglia and astrocytes) handle the brain's immunity and cleanup.
A leaky gut inflames the brain
Gut-brain axis: a leaky gut can lead to brain inflammation. Start with an anti-inflammatory diet.
When the glymphatic system runs well, waste drains away and your head feels refreshed.
